skill.name: ios-debugger-agent
skill.description: Use XcodeBuildMCP to build, run, launch, inspect, and debug iOS apps on a booted simulator.
skill.summary: Debug iOS simulator apps with XcodeBuildMCP build, launch, UI inspection, screenshots, and log capture workflows.
skill.author: Dimillian

security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives caused by markdown inline code references to XcodeBuildMCP tools and iOS simulator parameters. The skill guides authorized local simulator debugging, UI inspection, screenshots, and log capture without arbitrary command execution, network upload, or prompt injection content.

remediation.issue: Inline backtick tool names resemble shell execution to static analysis.
remediation.suggestion: Keep tool references explicit as MCP tool names and avoid adding shell command examples unless they are necessary and constrained.

remediation.issue: Screenshot and log capture features can expose app data during debugging.
remediation.suggestion: Remind users to run the skill only on authorized projects and avoid capturing sensitive production data in simulator sessions.

static_findings.snippet: - Call `mcp__XcodeBuildMCP__list_sims` and select the simulator with state `Booted`.
- If the app is already built and only launch is requested, use `mcp__XcodeBuildMCP__launch_app_sim`
- **Tap**: `mcp__XcodeBuildMCP__tap` (prefer `id` or `label`; use coordinates only if needed).
- **Gestures**: `mcp__XcodeBuildMCP__gesture` for common scrolls and edge swipes.
- Start logs: `mcp__XcodeBuildMCP__start_sim_log_cap` with the app bundle id.
- Stop logs: `mcp__XcodeBuildMCP__stop_sim_log_cap` and summarize important lines.
- For console output, set `captureConsole: true` and relaunch if required.
- If build fails, ask whether to retry with `preferXcodebuild: true`.
- If UI elements are not hittable, re-run `describe_ui` after layout changes.

content.value_statement: iOS simulator debugging often requires many separate build, launch, UI, and log steps. This skill gives Claude a clear XcodeBuildMCP workflow for inspecting app behavior in one guided session.
actual_capabilities: Finds a booted iOS simulator before running simulator actions.
Sets XcodeBuildMCP session defaults for project, scheme, and simulator.
Builds and runs an iOS app on the selected simulator when requested.
Launches an already built simulator app when a full build is not needed.
Describes, taps, types, gestures, and screenshots simulator UI through MCP tools.
Starts and stops simulator log capture and summarizes important console output.
limitations: Requires XcodeBuildMCP tools to be installed and available in the session.
Requires a booted simulator, unless the user explicitly asks to boot one.
Does not choose the correct scheme automatically when the project has ambiguous targets.
Does not replace unit tests, UI tests, or device testing on physical hardware.

use_cases.title: Validate a New iOS Screen
use_cases.description: Build and run the app, inspect the visible UI, and confirm that key elements appear on the simulator.

use_cases.title: Investigate Runtime Behavior
use_cases.description: Launch the app, capture console logs, interact with the UI, and summarize errors or warnings.

use_cases.title: Reproduce a Simulator Bug
use_cases.description: Follow a reported interaction path, use screenshots for confirmation, and collect simulator logs for diagnosis.

prompt_templates.title: Run the iOS App
prompt_templates.prompt: Run this iOS app on the booted simulator and tell me whether it launches successfully.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a basic simulator launch check.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect the Current Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the simulator tools to describe the current UI and point out anything that looks broken.
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer wants quick visual and accessibility-oriented inspection.

prompt_templates.title: Reproduce a Navigation Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Build and run the app, open the settings screen, tap the account option, and capture logs if the app fails.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate debugging flow with UI interaction and log capture.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Launch Regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Set the XcodeBuildMCP session defaults, run the Debug configuration, capture console output, and summarize likely causes of the launch failure.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced diagnosis that combines build, launch, and runtime evidence.

output_examples.input: Run the app and verify the home screen opens.
output_examples.output: The app built and launched on the booted simulator. The home screen is visible, and the main navigation controls are present.

output_examples.input: Check why tapping sign in does nothing.
output: The sign-in button is visible and hittable.
After tapping, the screen did not change.
The captured logs show a validation warning that should be investigated.

output_examples.input: Capture the current UI state for this bug report.
output_examples.output: The simulator screenshot confirms the error banner is displayed above the form. The UI description shows the retry button is available.

best_practices: Start with the booted simulator and confirm the target scheme before building.
Use UI description before tapping so interactions target visible elements.
Capture logs only for the app and summarize relevant lines instead of pasting noisy output.
anti_patterns: Do not run simulator actions without confirming a booted device exists.
Do not rely on coordinates when labels or element identifiers are available.
Do not treat simulator success as proof that behavior works on every physical device.

faq.question: Does this skill boot a simulator automatically?
faq.answer: No. It asks the user to boot one unless the user explicitly requests simulator booting.

faq.question: Can it build and run an iOS app?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses XcodeBuildMCP build and run tools when the project, scheme, and simulator are known.

faq.question: Can it interact with the app UI?
faq.answer: Yes. It can describe UI, tap elements, type text, perform gestures, and take screenshots through MCP tools.

faq.question: Can it capture logs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can start and stop simulator log capture for the app bundle and summarize important lines.

faq.question: Does it support physical iOS devices?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow is focused on a booted iOS simulator.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for automated tests?
faq.answer: No. It helps with manual debugging and verification, but tests should still cover expected behavior.
